review_notes: Read the whole file. The main bundled structure, coderivEquivTaylor (a ≃ₗ), and coderivations (a Submodule) are already present. The only candidate I found for a missing bundle is taylorComponent. Its zero/add/smul lemmas are stated separately. A grep of the repo shows taylorComponent_add and taylorComponent_smul are never used, and taylorComponent_zero is used in two places. The lemmas could be replaced by one linear map, but this is a modest, mostly cosmetic gain. I did not flag coderiv, because coderivEquivTaylor.symm already gives its linearity in F. I did not flag coderivSummand either. I did not compile any replacement.

findings.problem: taylorComponent b n is b ↦ (letter ∘ₗ b) ∘ₗ of n, which is linear in b. The file states this as three separate preservation lemmas (zero, add, smul) about an unbundled function. It therefore gets none of the LinearMap API, such as map_sum, map_neg, map_sub, or composition with the coderivEquivTaylor map. taylorComponent_add and taylorComponent_smul are not used anywhere in the repo. taylorComponent_zero is used in only two places.
findings.proposed_change: Bundle the map: define the linear map (ReducedTensorWords R M →ₗ[R] ReducedTensorWords R M) →ₗ[R] ((n : {n : ℕ // 0 < n}) → TensorPower R n.1 M →ₗ[R] M) as Pi.lift/LinearMap.pi of (LinearMap.lcomp-style) postcomposition with letter via LinearMap.compRight (letter R M) and precomposition with `of R M n`. Keep the pointwise `taylorComponent_apply` as a simp lemma. Then drop the zero/add/smul lemmas and use map_zero, map_add, map_smul and map_sum. Alternatively, keep the arity-wise function but define it from `LinearMap.compRight`/`LinearMap.lcomp` so linearity is inherited.
findings.benefit: Linearity becomes a single structured fact, and generic lemmas apply directly. Statements such as eq_zero_iff_taylorComponent_eq_zero become injectivity/kernel statements about a bundled linear map. This also matches the already bundled coderivEquivTaylor.
